title: Overall structure: match the two-part outline
subtitle: Text Structure and Purpose · 16 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **16 of the official questions in Text Structure and Purpose are this one** — 7 Easy, 5 Medium, 4 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Easy tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The question asks which choice best describes the overall structure of the text, and every answer choice follows the pattern 'It does X, then does Y.' The passage is usually a short informational text of 3-5 sentences with one clear turn.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write a 2-3 word label for the job of each sentence or chunk (introduces, explains, qualifies, challenges).
- 2) Find where the text turns, usually at 'However,' 'Still,' 'But,' or 'Thus.' 3) Check both halves of each choice against your labels.
- If either half is wrong, eliminate that choice.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Wrong choices usually get the first half right and the second half wrong.

The second half either describes a move the text never makes (a proposed solution, a history, several examples when there is only one) or gets the direction of the turn wrong (supports instead of complicates).
You pick a choice after reading only half of it.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
Wrong choices usually get the first half right and the second half wrong.

The second half either describes a move the text never makes (a proposed solution, a history, several examples when there is only one) or gets the direction of the turn wrong (supports instead of complicates).
